newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong sales may bolster corporate confidence--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Strong sales may bolster corporate confidence--BOJ.

text.p: Japanese corporate confidence may not worsen as much as expected if companies are able to achieve their sales forecasts, Kengo Inoue, an adviser for research and statistics to the Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) on Wednesday.
The BOJ earlier today announced its closely watched tankan survey of corporate confidence.
"If firms realise their sales plans as suggested by this survey, the diffusion index may not worsen as much as the survey suggests," Inoue said.
The tankan's key diffusion index for large manufacturers stood at plus two for March and minus one for June.
The survey also showed, however, that large manufacturers expected a 2.6 percent rise in sales in the fiscal year that started April 1.
"My reading is that the solid basis of the recovery is there. The results are mixed, but it's not that the recovery is faltering. It's very gradual but it's proceeding," he said.
